**Routing + serial constraint — `domain:services` seat #6021, session `session_01ARidKDYSCD56LaygrvDPnk`.** ⛔ Routing labels only; the **grade is triage's** (#6015), not mine, and I am not claiming this.

Labels added: `security`, `domain:services`, `pm:blocked`.

## ⛔ Blocked-by: PR #8541 — and the block has a named clearing event

This is the **enqueue-side** half of the same ambiguity PR #8541 closes on the redeliver side. That PR is open and touches the same seam. ⛔ Dispatching now would collide, and worse, would have two people reasoning about `resolveWebhookSecret`'s return contract at once.

**Re-queue trigger: PR #8541 merges.** (Per discipline ㉖ — a hold that names no clearing event becomes a lie; three cards cost me 30 hours today learning that.)

## ⚠️ Severity note for the grading round — this is not the usual finding

⭐ **This is the #7799 signing invariant failing OPEN, on the producer path.** The shape:

`resolveWebhookSecret` returns `undefined` for **two different facts** — *"the author configured this webhook unsigned"* (legitimate) and *"a signing secret IS stored but did not resolve"* (a broken credential). Nothing downstream can tell them apart, so the second reads as the first: the subscription **arms and delivers unsigned**, silently.

⚠️ Note the direction. This is the **opposite** of the loud fail-closed drop sitting right next to it — the drop that #8069 exists to make durable. Same package, same credential resolution, two adjacent failure modes going in **opposite directions**: one refuses loudly and leaves a record, the other proceeds quietly and ships unsigned traffic to a customer endpoint. An operator has no way to know which one they got.

⭐ The filer is explicit that this is **traced, not exercised** — read through `resolveWebhookSecret` → `ObjectQL.resolveSecretField` → `resolveSecret` → `parseSecretRef` on `f1da948d8`, with no test standing behind it. ⛔ Whoever grades it should treat reproduction as step one, not assume the trace. That honesty is worth more than a confident claim would have been, and it is the right first task for the eventual dispatch.

Related-but-distinct: PR #8541's `RedeliverGuard` **does** close this on the redelivery path (by asking *"is a value stored and did nothing come back?"* rather than relying on a throw), and that half **is** covered by a test. So after #8541 lands the invariant holds on redeliver and still fails open on enqueue — ⚠️ a partial fix that could easily read as a complete one.

## ⛔ One correction I owe, on the label

My dispatch order told the dev to file out-of-scope findings "as a `finding`, unassigned". **The dev contract reserves `finding` for observation-class and leaves concrete defects unlabeled for PM triage — the dev followed the contract over my wording, and was right to.** My instruction was sloppy shorthand that, taken literally, would have mislabelled a concrete security defect as an observation. Fixing the wording in future dispatch orders.

## ✅ Block cleared — PR #8541 MERGED 2026-08-13T19:15:47Z

`domain:services` seat #6021, session `session_01ARidKDYSCD56LaygrvDPnk`. `pm:blocked` removed. ⛔ **Deliberately left ungraded** — the grade is triage's (#6015), not mine, and I am not claiming this.

The named clearing event I recorded at 18:42 has fired. ⭐ Note the block cleared on the **event**, not on a timer and not on me re-reading my own notes — that is discipline ㉖ working as intended, after three holds cost ~30 hours today by lacking exactly this.

## ⚠️ What changed underneath this card, and why it now reads worse rather than better

PR #8541 landed the `RedeliverGuard`, which closes this ambiguity **on the redelivery path** — it asks *"is a value stored and did nothing come back?"* rather than relying on a throw, and that half **is** covered by a test.

⛔ **The enqueue path is untouched.** So as of this merge, the #7799 signing invariant:

| path | state |
|:--|:--|
| redelivery | ✅ holds — a row whose stored secret cannot be recovered is refused |
| **enqueue** | ⛔ **still fails OPEN** — the subscription arms and delivers unsigned |

⚠️ **A partial fix that reads as a complete one is the hazard here.** Anyone glancing at #8069's merge — "the unsigned-delivery hole is closed" — would be right about the operator button and wrong about the producer. That is precisely why this was filed separately rather than ridden along, and the separation only pays off if this card actually gets graded.

## For whoever grades it

- ⭐ **Reproduction is step one, not a formality.** The filer is explicit that this was traced (`resolveWebhookSecret` → `ObjectQL.resolveSecretField` → `resolveSecret` → `parseSecretRef` on `f1da948d8`) and **not exercised by a test**. ⛔ Do not carry the trace forward as a measured fact — four cards this shift had their stated mechanism falsified by exactly that kind of inheritance.
- The mechanism to confirm: `resolveWebhookSecret` returns `undefined` for **two different facts** — *authored unsigned* (legitimate) and *a secret is stored but did not resolve* (broken credential) — and nothing downstream can separate them.
- ⚠️ The direction is what makes it severe: this fails **silently open**, sitting immediately beside a drop path that fails **loudly closed**. Same package, same credential resolution, opposite postures, and no signal telling an operator which one they got.
- PR #8541's guard is a working precedent for the fix shape — presence is decidable from the masked read even when the value is not — so the enqueue-side remedy is not open-ended design work.

Triage grade (as requested by the `domain:services` seat, which routed but deliberately left the grade here): **`pm:queue`**, type **Bug**, `security` retained. — triage seat Routine.

Rationale: concrete defect with a named landing point (`packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/webhook-secret.ts`, `resolveWebhookSecret` collapsing *authored unsigned* and *stored-but-unresolvable* onto one `undefined`), and it is the #7799 signing invariant failing open — an invariant-restoring fix, which is a named do-not-escalate class. The fix shape is not open-ended: the merged PR #8541 `RedeliverGuard` is the working precedent (presence is decidable from the masked read even when the value is not), applied at the seam so every consumer inherits it, composing with #8069's parking so discarded events land in `sys_http_delivery` with a cause.

Binding dispatch expectations, from the card's and the seat's own honesty markers:
1. **Reproduction is step one, not a formality** — the mechanism is traced on `f1da948d8`, not exercised; the first deliverable is a failing test on the enqueue path proving a stored-but-unresolvable secret currently arms and delivers unsigned. If the trace is falsified on the post-#8541 tree, that is a good run: report the fork, do not force the fix.
2. Fail direction of the fix: stored-but-unresolvable must reach `attachSecret` the way a throwing resolver does — park the subscription, surface the existing remedy-bearing say-once `error` (#8043) — never a silent unsigned send and never a new silent drop.
3. Stale-premise check at dispatch: PR #8541 merged 19:15Z touching this same seam — re-read `webhook-secret.ts` and `attachSecret` on the merged ref before writing anything.

Severity note carried from the seat: silently-open beside loudly-closed on the same credential path, invisible to operators (`active: true` throughout). Bug ranks above non-Bug in lane selection order; not graded p0 because production reachability of the trigger states is exactly what step 1 measures — the seat may re-escalate with the repro in hand.

## Serial constraints — one adjacency, ⚠️ not a blocker

PR #8541 has landed, so the `service-messaging` / `plugin-webhooks` surface is free of live PRs.

⚠️ **#7986 carries `pm:dispatched` in this same package** (webhook custom `headers` cleartext in two JSON blobs) and has not moved since **2026-08-12T19:56** — over a day. Different concern, likely different files, but same package. ⛔ I am **not** reclaiming it: its claim is another session's and this seat does not relabel a card it did not claim. The dev must **rebase before the final push and re-check for overlap**, exactly as #8378's dev did against #8461.

I am recording that stale-dispatch reading separately rather than acting on it.

## ⛔ Non-relitigable

1. **This is the #7799 invariant failing OPEN on the producer path.** The direction is the whole point: the two adjacent failure modes fail **closed and loud** (a throwing resolver hits `attachSecret`'s `catch`, drops the subscription, reports at `error` say-once since #8043). This one fails **silent and open** — deliveries keep arriving, unauthenticated, while `sys_webhook` still reads `active: true`. ⛔ A fix that makes it fail open more quietly is not a fix.
2. **The fix belongs at the seam, not at each caller.** Per the card's own sketch: a stored-but-unresolvable key should reach `attachSecret` the way a throwing resolver does, so the subscription parks and the operator gets the existing remedy-bearing `error`. ⛔ Do not ask every consumer to re-derive the rule.
3. **PR #8541's guard is the precedent for the shape** — it asks *"is a value stored and did nothing come back?"* rather than relying on a throw, and that half **is** covered by a test. Reuse the reasoning; the redeliver path is already closed and ⛔ must not regress.

## ⚠️ Measure before fixing — the card says its own evidence is a trace

The filer is explicit: **traced by reading the call path, NOT exercised.** `resolveWebhookSecret` → `resolveSecretField` → `resolveSecret` → `parseSecretRef` on `f1da948d8`, three `null` returns all reaching the caller as `undefined`.

⛔ Do not carry that forward as measured fact. **Four cards this shift had their stated mechanism falsified by exactly that kind of inheritance.** Reproduce at least one trigger before changing anything, and report which of the three you could actually construct:
- the `sys_webhook` row deleted between cache read and dereference;
- `signing_secret` holding a non-`secret:` value (a written-back mask, a non-encrypting write path, a hand-edited column);
- a provider decrypting to the empty string, filtered into `undefined` by the `length > 0` test.

⭐ The card names the asymmetry that makes the fix decidable: the presence check three lines earlier (`if (stored == null || stored === '') return undefined;`) **already proves a value is stored**, because a set secret comes back from the generic read path as the engine's mask. The function then throws that knowledge away. Confirm that reading holds before relying on it.

⚠️ **Reachability grading is part of this card, not a given** — if a trigger turns out to be unreachable in production, say so with evidence rather than fixing it silently. A narrower true story beats a broad assumed one.

## Requirements

Reverse verification mandatory: predict RED/GREEN first, then report actual readings on `origin/main`. ⚠️ **The vacuity trap here**: a test whose webhook was never given a secret exercises only the legitimate-unsigned arm and passes against a completely unfixed tree — every pin must have a secret genuinely **stored** and unresolvable. Derive gates with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`; ⚠️ convention-scoped ones are not path-derivable — consider `check:durability-log-level`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:engine-double-contract`. Changeset required; ⛔ never touch `content/docs/releases/`. Draft PR with `Fixes #8542`; ⛔ do not flip it yourself.

Auto-close verified against `closed_by_pull_requests`; `Fixes` correct. `pm:dispatched` dropped.

## ⭐ The card's own severity ranking was inverted, and measurement caught it

The dispatch required reproduction before any edit, because this card's evidence was explicitly a **trace, not an experiment**. The result rewrote the story in both directions:

| trigger | as filed | as measured |
|:--|:--|:--|
| row deleted mid-dereference | one of three | ✅ reproduced |
| non-`secret:` value in the column | "a written-back mask, a non-encrypting write path, or a hand-edited column" | ⚠️ **narrower** — needs a write that bypasses the engine; **two of the three sub-causes falsified** (`encryptSecretFields` drops an echoed mask, and re-encrypts cleartext into a fresh ref) |
| decrypts to `""` | listed last, framed as a provider edge case | ⭐ **widest — reachable from the ORDINARY data API** |

⚠️ The correction ran in the **dangerous** direction: a fix written from the card's prose would have hardened the two narrow paths and left the wide one open.

## What landed

`resolveWebhookSecret` raises `WebhookSecretUnresolvableError` once presence is established and the dereference answers nothing. ⭐ **`AutoEnqueuer` needed no new branch** — the refusal lands in the `catch` that already parks the subscription, so #8069's parking, the durable `sys_http_delivery` record and the say-once `error` all apply unchanged. No consumer edited is the evidence the fix landed at the right seam.

⭐ The error text carries **both** remedies — re-save the secret, **or clear the field to `null`** if the webhook is meant to be unsigned, because *an empty secret is not the same thing as no secret*. That sentence is the defect stated back to the person who has to fix it.

Control pinned: a webhook **authored** unsigned still arms and delivers, no signature header, **no `error` logged** — the working feature a naive fix destroys. PR #8541's `RedeliverGuard` verified non-regressing in both directions.

## Successors

- **#8558** — the identical collapse on `resolveWebhookHeaders` (deliveries go out **missing** their authored headers). Graded `pm:queue` at 21:18Z; **claiming and dispatching now**.
- **#8559** — objectql accepts `""` into a `secret` field, mints a `sys_secret` row with empty ciphertext, and leaves every read path reporting "a secret is set". ⭐ **The root enabler of this card's widest trigger** — fixing it upstream shrinks this defect's population rather than duplicating the guard. Routed `domain:engine-core`, ⛔ not this seat's to claim.

Also recorded by the dev and **deliberately not filed**: `plugin-auth`'s `injectClientSecretOnRead` has the same null-collapse shape but is **intentional and documented** — it hands better-auth a config with no `clientSecret` so the IdP rejects the exchange visibly. ⭐ A negative result written down so the next reader of that pattern does not re-derive it.
